summary: Ran M4-S02 (sla, owner metadata-builder) end to end. The step was in build_plan.py next --milestone M4, was claimed running, and the owning agent was executed inline per AGENT.md Step 6 (this host runs the builder inline, as every step of this build has). All five declared outputs were written under artefacts/M4-S02/ plus an undeclared deploy-order.md; check-outputs returned ok:true and 4/4 XML files parse. The owning agent returned an ambiguity it could not resolve without inventing metadata, so the step was set blocked with --blocked-reason ambiguity rather than built: the step's declared acceptance-test checker exits 1 under --strict on two W4 findings that cannot be cleared because no step in the plan builds a Workflow file and no clarification names a milestone notification. Nothing was deployed, no gate was approved, and no file was written outside the build directory.
confidence_rationale: build-step-runner Step 9: LOW because the step was set blocked. Every other HIGH condition held - the step was in next, all required inputs resolved from plan.json, check-outputs exited 0, both envelopes validate, and nothing landed outside artefacts/M4-S02/.

process_observations.observation: Every required input of the owning agent resolved from plan.json alone - no value was taken from the invocation brief, and the one place the brief and the plan could have diverged (the 67.0 package.xml version) was cross-checked against the build's own artefacts rather than accepted on the brief's word.

The blocked exit was reached with all five declared outputs on disk and check-outputs ok:true, so the human sees exactly what would ship rather than an empty directory - the same shape M4-S01's blocked run left behind.

The step's acceptance test adds --strict to promote W3 into an assertion and thereby also promotes W4, which no artefact this plan scopes can satisfy - a planning defect that only surfaces at build time, because the planner's fixture was built from the skill's own examples and those carry workflow actions.

check-outputs returned ok:true on a step that cannot pass its own declared checker, so a green check-outputs is not evidence a step is buildable - it adjudicates presence and parseability of declared paths only.

deploy-order.md is written on every metadata-builder run by contract but is declared in no step's outputs[] anywhere in this build, so it is reported as an undeclared artefact on every single step - the fifth consecutive time, after M3-S01 through M3-S04 and M4-S01.
M4-S03 and M4-S04 both remain runnable and neither depends on M4-S02, so M4 can continue while this block is adjudicated - but the milestone gate cannot close until it is.
Once a human picks one of the three ways forward, the step returns to pending and is re-run rather than tested.
process_observations.followup_reason: Because it owns the declared acceptance tests and is the next stage the moment this step reaches built - but not before, since a blocked step has nothing to test.
